clue.text: Air force officer learners do badly — one of four gets in

indicators.note: gets in says one piece enters and sits inside the other
done badly, the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a quad is short for a quadruplet, one of four born together

explanation.surface: A complaint that trainee pilots perform poorly, with one of a set of quadruplets joining them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the learners' letters to SRONLEADER, and 'gets in' slots the quadruplet in after the opening S.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rank in the RAF, an officer commanding a flying squadron.

clue.text: She became animated when given smack

definitions.text: She became animated when given smack

parts.words: She became animated when given smack
parts.note: the fairy-tale princess wakes, becoming lively, when given a kiss (a smack); she was also the subject of a Disney animated film

explanation.surface: Seems to describe someone reviving after a dose of heroin (smack).
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' suggests a slap or the drug heroin, but here it is a smacking kiss; 'animated' means both brought to life and drawn as a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The princess of the fairy tale sleeps under a spell until a prince's kiss wakes her.

clue.text: Free bananas at lunch

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An offer of complimentary fruit at the midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a door or gate is to release its catch so it opens.

clue.text: Reader, perhaps, or one making presentation

parts.note: a reader is a senior university lecturer, an example of a don
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a book reader or a presenter is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a giver, someone who presents a gift.

clue.text: Thoroughly beat, not in form

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Someone soundly defeated because they are off their game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like fitness, as in 'not in form'; here it is a school form, a CLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass rivals is to be so superior that they are utterly defeated.

clue.text: Gold added to state carriage

indicators.note: added to puts the gold symbol on after the other piece

parts.note: a land is a country or state
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A ceremonial state coach decorated with gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state carriage' reads as one phrase, but 'state' is LAND and the definition is 'carriage' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with a folding top.

clue.text: Pharaoh's name meant "hope" when translated

indicators.note: translating changes the words' form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Egyptologist explaining that a king's name signified hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Egyptian kings of the Eighteenth Dynasty bore this name.

clue.text: One following leading characters of excellence pre-eminent in the past

indicators.note: leading characters are the initial letters of the following words

parts.note: what is gone is in the past

explanation.surface: Describes someone who once followed excellence and pre-eminence long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but its first letter is needed too: 'leading characters of' takes E, P and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigone is a lesser imitator or follower of a great artist or thinker.

clue.text: Going by window not refastened I fall out

indicators.note: the letters fall out of order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles through a window they failed to fasten again.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenestration is throwing someone, or going, out of a window.

clue.text: Duke has capital in New Zealand, for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means most of the word is kept, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: Wellington is the capital city of New Zealand

explanation.surface: A nobleman owns a house in the New Zealand capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' suggests the Duke of Wellington; it is Duke Ellington, the jazz bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke was the nickname of the American jazz composer and bandleader Edward Kennedy Ellington.

clue.text: English team the French cast out

parts.note: XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An English side dropped by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person banished, driven out of their homeland.

clue.text: Safe time to look around

indicators.note: around says the look word goes round the time letter

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Advice that it is safe to glance about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like an adjective meaning secure; it is a strongbox, PETER in criminal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In old criminal slang a peter is a strongbox that safe-crackers blow open.

clue.text: Hateful school-mate caught out being horrible

indicators.note: being horrible signals the remaining letters turned into a nasty mess, an anagram
out says the cricket letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A nasty classmate caught misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from SCHOOLMATE, leaving SHOOLMATE, which 'being horrible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome is detestable, arousing disgust and dislike.

clue.text: Philosophy with nothing to offer its followers?

definitions.text: Philosophy with nothing to offer its followers?

parts.words: Philosophy with nothing to offer its followers?
parts.note: a doctrine that holds nothing has value or meaning literally offers its adherents nothing

explanation.surface: A sneer at a school of thought that gives its disciples nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from Latin nihil, nothing, so the joke is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihilism rejects all moral principles and holds that life is without meaning.

clue.text: See female smile in this opera

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see, behold
a hen is a female bird
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a woman smiling during an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's romantic opera about the swan knight bears this title.

clue.text: Goddess at that time among leaders of Aesir

indicators.note: among puts the time word in between the leading letters
leaders are the first letters of the word

parts.note: then means at that time

explanation.surface: A goddess once dwelt among the chiefs of the Norse gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' gives the first two letters, A and E, of AESIR (the Norse gods) and THEN goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Perfectly happy composer getting nearly drunk

parts.note: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A composer who is merry and close to intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful means in a state of perfect joy.

clue.text: Bed a girl

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Reads as a crude instruction about a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Queen's favourite racing event in sound only

indicators.note: in sound only means the word is matched by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: a rally is a motor race over public roads

explanation.surface: A monarch's preferred motor race, heard only on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Raleigh was a favourite of Queen Elizabeth I; his name is often said like RALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Raleigh was the courtier much favoured by Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Disrespectful and loud abuse to criticise team leader

parts.note: F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud
lip is cheeky, abusive talk
to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rude, noisy tirade attacking the captain of a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means lacking proper seriousness or respect.

clue.text: Greed shown by girl over pudding.

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the girl's name above the pudding

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice pudding is a classic dessert

explanation.surface: A girl greedily eyeing a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth.

clue.text: Husband wearing armour that's provided by Grace

indicators.note: wearing says the armour piece is put on around the husband letter

parts.note: tanks are armoured vehicles, armour in military terms

explanation.surface: A husband in armour provided by a woman called Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a woman's name; it is the grace said before meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying grace is giving thanks to God for a meal.

clue.text: Tree with liana growing wild to such an extent

indicators.note: growing wild means the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: thus means so, to such an extent

explanation.surface: A tree overgrown by a rampant climbing vine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailanthus is a genus of trees including the tree of heaven.

clue.text: Portuguese explorer finished off this lizard?

indicators.note: finished off means only the finishing part of the name is used

parts.note: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who reached India by sea

explanation.surface: Wonders whether the great explorer killed a lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished off' looks like killed, but it takes the end of VASCO DA GAMA, the final A GAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agama is an Old World lizard.

clue.text: A professional name for the stage

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: Seems to describe an actor's professional stage name.
explanation.definitionFit: The apron is the part of a theatre stage in front of the curtain.

clue.text: One who persists and runs into a row

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A stubborn person who charges into an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel; it is a line of seats, a TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who keeps trying, never giving up.

clue.text: Wrongly interfere with it, dropping one queen for another

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are set out in the wrong order
dropping says the queen's letters are removed from the words

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A warning not to meddle, as one monarch is swapped for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes ER from INTERFERE IT and 'Wrongly' rearranges the rest; 'another' is another queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an Egyptian queen, wife of Akhenaten, so a queen other than ER.

clue.text: Product of Taiwanese light industry?

parts.note: light industry is read as the industry making lights, an item from the Far East giving light

explanation.surface: A trade report on goods from Taiwan's light manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light industry' means small-goods manufacturing, but here it is a maker of lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper lantern of Far Eastern design, also a plant with papery orange calyces.
